claims.text: Brittle behavior in initially single-phase HEAs emerges primarily when grain-boundary chemical ordering or clustering occurs.
Grain-boundary chemical ordering or clustering induces nanoscale precipitation or phase separation.
Nanoscale precipitation or phase separation at grain boundaries causes embrittlement in HEAs.
In conventional alloys, grain-boundary segregation and coarse intermetallic precipitation dominate toughness loss.
The degree of local ordering in an HEA depends on its configurational entropy.
The degree of local ordering and its effect on toughness depend on atomic-diffusion kinetics during service or thermal exposure.
The initial HEA is single-phase, has a homogeneous elemental distribution, and has fine grains.
Thermal exposure or mechanical loading promotes atomic diffusion and potential local ordering at grain boundaries.
The proposed mechanism applies under tensile or impact loading from ambient temperature to approximately 300–800°C.
Local reduction of configurational entropy at grain boundaries enables atomic clustering or ordering.
Ordered clusters at grain boundaries act as nucleation sites for brittle phases.
Grain-boundary ordering or clustering can impede grain-boundary sliding.
Nucleation of brittle phases or impeded grain-boundary sliding reduces toughness.
Relative to the initial baseline, HEA toughness decreases only if nanoscale ordering or precipitation occurs at grain boundaries.
Toughness degradation in the HEA is less pronounced than in a comparable conventional alloy.
The onset of brittleness in HEAs is delayed and less severe than in conventional alloys.
Prolonged thermal exposure or extreme loading can still cause brittle behavior in HEAs.
The initial single-phase HEA baseline has high toughness and ductility and lacks grain-boundary precipitation or ordering.
The hypothesis is limited to conditions that do not induce macroscopic phase separation or coarse precipitation.
The hypothesis breaks down if the alloy loses its single-phase character or external impurities are introduced.
